couplingHotspots.description: Kernel core <-> learning layer is bidirectional: strategy.ts and supervise-surface.ts import supervise/{driver-executor,model-policy,runtime,supervisor,supervise,completion-gate,trace-source,trace-evidence,types}, while supervise/worktree-fanout.ts imports personify/combinators + wave-types and supervise/stop-rules.ts imports ../anytime. supervise-surface.ts:10-15 documents living above supervise to dodge the cycle, but worktree-fanout and stop-rules already close it in the other direction.

Kernel <-> retained-run is bidirectional: supervise/types.ts, scope.ts, run-layout.ts, interactive-admission.ts, worker-interactive.ts, interactive-worker.ts import retained-* types/functions, while retained-run-start.ts, retained-interactive.ts, retained-interactive-handle.ts import supervise/snapshot (detachedSnapshot).

The `/graph` engine reaches into supervise internals rather than its public surface: it imports maxSeqOf/sumMeasuredSpendFromEvents/uncertainSpawnBudgets from supervise/supervisor.ts, workerFromBackend/supervisorAgent, finalizer internals, GraphEdgeCapError from supervise/graph.ts, and mcp/tools/coordination types; supervise/graph.ts does not import the engine.

Corpus/Outcome types are owned by personify/wave-types + personify/types but consumed by observe.ts, harvest-corpus.ts and strategy.ts outside personify, so the observer/flywheel write side and the persona read side are split across two module trees with the type home in one of them.

define-leaderboard spans both loop substrates: it wires the round-synchronous loop (loopDispatch + naiveRetryDriver + isTerminalDecision semantics from run-loop) and agent-eval's runProfileMatrix, while strategy/personify run on the reactive Scope — the two-substrate split index.ts:20-25 documents lands inside one facade.

The /kernel barrel re-exports types and values from ../mcp/tools/coordination, ../durable/spawn-journal, ../otel-export and ../mcp/worktree-harness, so the kernel's public surface includes the MCP subpath's coordination vocabulary.

Every analyst/author call site builds its own ExecutorConfig and goes through profileChatClient: strategy.ts (analystChat + observe), strategy-author.ts, strategy-evolution.ts (reproducer summary), audit-intent.ts, run-benchmark.ts (preflight), observe.ts — six entry points into one adapter with the router config literal repeated at three of them.

complexityHotspots.why: createCoordinationTools is one 2291-line closure (1417-3707) holding ~40 inner closures, 13 tool handlers, and the analyst/continuity/journal/peer-mail/escalation state machines; the file is 3741 LOC (>1500).

CoordinationToolsOptions has 27 fields, 24 optional, several encoding behavior switches by sentinel (awaitTimeoutMs <= 0 = unbounded at 2748; maxLiveWorkers <= 0 = uncapped at 2604-2618; maxDefinedAnalysts <= 0 = no cap at 2554; redactJournal: false = opt out at 902) plus opt-in seams (replaySettlements, watchWorkers, peerMail, preflightSpawn, resolveSpawnProfile, escalateQuestion, priorQuestions/priorEscalations/priorJournal/priorAnalystDefinitions).

spawn_worker tool definition + handler is 258 lines (2764-3021); the refusal payload is a triple-nested ternary over res.reason (2993-3015) duplicating the same sentences in `reason` and `hint` (2867-2872, 2997-3015).

runLocalHarness is 255 lines (603-857) forked on the boolean `codexReproducible` at 611, 614, 620, 640, 651, 677, 680, 813, 832; the non-reproducible branch is a 15-field stub object (659-674) shaped to mirror isolateCodexHome's return. File is 1791 LOC.

isolateCodexHome is 161 lines returning a 14-field record; collectCodexExecutionEvidence (897-1036, 140 lines) embeds shell (935-950) and Python (973-979, 989) probe programs as string literals; runCodexProbe (1086-1196, 111 lines) repeats the runLocalHarness spawn lifecycle.

detachedSessionDelegate is 120 lines with two boolean forks (variants <= 1 at 230; ctx.detachedSessionRef !== undefined at 239) producing three execution paths (detached single, streamed single, fanout) that each call pickCoderWinner/settle with their own report() bookkeeping.

execute (445-509) and driveResume (559-614) repeat the terminal-transition block four times (492-497, 500-505, 579-599, 604-610); `currentStatus()` (715) exists only to defeat TypeScript narrowing after the `record.status = 'running'` assignment (comment at 488-491).

RunWorktreeHarnessOptions carries 17 fields including three test seams (runGit, runHarness, runCommand) and two Codex-only flags (codexReproducible, codexReadDeniedPaths) that throw for every other harness (local-harness.ts:611-622); spawnProfiledHarness (481-530) takes a 12-field bag.

The runCommand adapter (92-108) accepts `timeoutMs` and does not pass it on; defaultRunPostCheck (240-278) uses the fixed DEFAULT_POSTCHECK_TIMEOUT_MS and a leader-only kill, so the documented `postCheckTimeoutMs` option (42-43) is inert for the default runner. Not covered by tests/mcp/in-process-executor.test.ts.

parseCoderEvents tolerates three terminal payload shapes plus a transcript scan for the last fenced JSON block (139-165, 227-261) and returns an all-false empty CoderOutput (158-164) when nothing matches, leaving the validator to reject rather than reporting 'no result decoded'.

Hand-written validators (114-290, ~175 lines) mirror the JSON Schema at 58-109 field-by-field; the same pattern repeats in delegate-feedback.ts:83-149 and delegation-history.ts:57-92, so every schema change is made twice.

Root files and the runtime/ subsystem import each other: root → runtime (src/errors.ts:33 → runtime/retained-run-types; src/backends.ts:10 → runtime/turn-input) and runtime → root (stream-agent-turn.ts:62-73 → ../backends, ../errors, ../sessions, ../types; run-loop.ts:29-31 → ../errors, ../runtime-hooks, ../types; sandbox-run.ts:36-37 → ../runtime-hooks; runtime/types.ts:25-26 → ../runtime-hooks, ../runtime-run; router-client.ts:21, sandbox-lineage.ts:43, stdio-mcp-client.ts:42, codex-rollout-store.ts:51, runtime/tool-loop.ts:12 → ../errors). src/errors.ts, meant as the package error taxonomy, depends on a deep retained-run type module.

The turn kernel reaches into retained-run and supervise internals: stream-agent-turn.ts imports awaitAbortable from retained-run-binding (74), executableAgentProfileSnapshot from supervise/executable-spec (85), six receipt builders from supervise/materialization (86-95), model-policy (96-100) and supervise/types (101-110); assertExactExecutorDeclaration (272-342) hard-codes backend strings 'router' | 'router-tools' | 'bridge' | 'bridge-worktree' and reads `declaration.plan` fields owned by supervise/runtime.ts executors.

supervise/runtime.ts is the hub that consumes every transport module's non-public exports: router-client (99: routerChatWithUsage/routerChatWithTools/streamRouterChatWithTools/readPromptCache/routerTransportAttemptsFromError), codex-rollout-store (73), environment-provider (81), util (123: roundBoxMinutes, cloneTokenUsage, unmeteredSpend). loop-dispatch.ts couples the sandbox kernel to agent-eval's campaign contract (type imports from @tangle-network/agent-eval/campaign at 37-43) and to supervise/supervise (47) and model-identity (45); it re-implements cost-receipt mapping (183-226) that supervise/runtime also computes for its journal.

assertExactExecutorDeclaration switches on backend string literals ('router' | 'router-tools' | 'bridge' | 'bridge-worktree') and casts `declaration.plan` to ad-hoc shapes (289-293, 331) instead of a typed declaration.

runAgentRounds is 257 lines (161-417) and executeIteration 231 lines (685-915); RunBatchArgs carries 17 fields (601-643); three mutually exclusive box-ownership modes (default teardown / onWorkerBox / lineage) are expressed as boolean/optional forks (203-217, 456-460, 886-902); `streaming: 'sse'|'poll'` is a fourth fork (768-778).

environmentAsSandboxInstance (164 lines) and sandboxInstanceAsEnvironment (169 lines, 1094-1262) conditionally spread 8-10 optional methods each based on `has*` duck-typing guards (2307-2347) and return `box as unknown as SandboxInstance` (1091).

buildLoopSpanNodes is 197 lines of a hand-rolled state machine over string-keyed payloads (`rec`/`num`/`str` coercions 505-510) with three closures; the file also hosts an unrelated HTTP ingest client (787-897).
runToolLoop (139 lines) and streamToolLoop (143 lines) are parallel implementations; each has four early-return stop branches (deadline/backstop/stuck-loop/budget) that must be kept in sync.
structuralRollout's inner strategy body is 161 lines with nested sample and repair loops, an inline Candidate interface (562-569), and receipt bookkeeping mixed with selection.

collectProviderModels (103 lines) has eight `return { kind: 'unknown' }` exits and per-attempt snapshot-kind tracking; supervisedTreeModelForDispatch (264-294) then re-reduces it and ignores its `rootProfile` parameter (268 `void rootProfile`).
runAgentTaskStream is 164 lines with the success and failure paths each emitting and persisting four events by hand (289-313, 340-365).
RuntimeTelemetryOptions is seven independent booleans (35-47) consulted across ~25 branches (105-310, 400-457); sanitizeRuntimeStreamEvent is a 150-line type switch.

ExecCtx has 9 optional fields including four observer channels (hooks, traceEmitter, onSandboxEvent, runHandle) and two unread ones (traceId, parentSpanId); the promptOptions doc block (626-647) enumerates per-client key refusals that live in other files.

Usage parsing spans 1841-1976 (six functions) plus tokenUsageData 1621, usageSandboxEvent 1591 and the usage branching inside sandboxEventFromEnvironmentEvent 1488-1518 — nine places deciding where a token count lives.
